about: Case study timeline data, written by scripts/build_case_study_timeline.py from data/case_studies.yaml; do not edit. Row keys: p study path, t title, k kind, s and e the period (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD; e null while ongoing), cs and ce the core period when the study names one, y the year the study is placed under, sec sectors, cve CVE ids named in the study, act ATT&CK groups [id, name], tag tags, pdf and pptx download links, ev dated key events [date, label]. Rows are newest first.

rows.t: The Year 2018 in Intrusions: A Dated Record
ev: Google Project Zero publishes the speculative-execution flaws CVE-2017-5753, CVE-2017-5715 and CVE-2017-5754 (Spectre and Meltdown)
Olympic Destroyer disrupts PyeongChang Winter Olympics systems during the opening ceremony; recovery within about 12 hours
The UK and the White House attribute the June 2017 NotPetya attack to the Russian military
GitHub is offline for five minutes under a memcached-reflected DDoS peaking at 1.35 Tbps
US-UK alert TA18-106A on Russian state-sponsored exploitation of routers and switches; NIST releases CSF 1.1
Talos publishes VPNFilter on at least 500,000 devices; DOJ obtains orders for the FBI to seize a C2 domain
Special Counsel indictment of 12 GRU officers for 2016 election interference (allegations)
DOJ unseals the Park Jin Hyok complaint (Sony, Bangladesh Bank, WannaCry 2.0); OFAC designates Park and his employer
Facebook discloses the View As breach and resets access tokens for almost 50 million accounts
DOJ unseals the SamSam indictment; OFAC designates two Iran-based exchangers and publishes bitcoin addresses for the first time
Marriott discloses access to the Starwood network since 2014: up to about 500 million guests
DOJ unseals the APT10 indictment and the UK and allies attribute APT 10 to China's MSS

rows.t: The Year 2017 in Intrusions: A Dated Record
ev: WikiLeaks publishes Vault 7 Part 1, "Year Zero", 8,761 documents it says came from the CIA
Microsoft publishes MS17-010, fixing the SMBv1 flaws later used by WannaCry and NotPetya
First backdoored M.E.Doc update goes out through the vendor's own update channel
TA17-117A: intrusions at IT service providers reach customers in at least 12 countries
WannaCry spreads through SMBv1 in over 150 countries; at least 81 NHS trusts in England disrupted
Equifax intruders begin extracting data from the online dispute portal
NotPetya surfaces through M.E.Doc and spreads worldwide
Kaspersky publishes ShadowPad in NetSarang products; backdoored CCleaner 5.33 released
Equifax announces an incident affecting about 143 million US consumers
Bad Rabbit spreads through compromised websites serving a fake Flash Player update
Mandiant publishes TRITON, used to reprogram Triconex safety controllers
The United States, with the UK, Australia, Canada, New Zealand and Japan, attributes WannaCry to North Korea

rows.t: The Shadow Brokers and Vault 7: The NSA and CIA Tool Leaks, 2016 to 2017
ev: A CIA developer restores revoked privileges, copies the CCI tool-development archives and deletes hundreds of log files
The Shadow Brokers leak begins: a bitcoin auction of "Equation Group" files and a free sample archive
Cisco publishes ASA advisories for CVE-2016-6366 and CVE-2016-6367 from the leaked firewall exploits
WikiLeaks begins Vault 7 with "Year Zero", CIA Center for Cyber Intelligence material
Microsoft publishes MS17-010, fixing six SMBv1 CVEs, a month before the Windows release
The Shadow Brokers post "Lost in Translation" with Windows exploits; MSRC maps them to existing fixes the next day
WannaCry spreads with the leaked SMBv1 exploit; at least 81 of 236 NHS trusts in England infected
NotPetya begins in Ukraine through M.E.Doc, spreading by credential theft and two SMB exploits
CIA WikiLeaks Task Force final report finds security on the development network "woefully lax"
WikiLeaks begins Vault 8 with source code for the CIA Hive tool
Joshua Schulte convicted on eight counts at retrial over the Vault 7 theft
Schulte sentenced to 40 years

rows.t: The Year 2016 in Intrusions: A Dated Record
ev: An attacker in Bangladesh Bank's SWIFT system attempts $951 million in transfers; $81 million is not recovered
TA16-091A: Locky in hospitals in the US, New Zealand and Germany; Samas into healthcare networks through web servers
Stolen DCCC credentials used to enter the DCCC network, the DNC reached on 18 April (indictment allegation)
No More Ransom launches
Cisco is alerted to Shadow Brokers material claiming Equation Group exploits for PIX and ASA
Citizen Lab publishes the Trident report; Apple ships iOS 9.3.5, 24 and 25 August
A DDoS of about 620 Gbps hits KrebsOnSecurity; Akamai absorbs it
Yahoo discloses the theft of data from at least 500 million accounts in late 2014
DHS and ODNI joint statement on Russian-directed email compromises
Shamoon 2's hardcoded wipe time against at least one Saudi organization
Part of Kyiv without power for about one hour; ESET judges Industroyer's use highly probable
Sanctions, expulsions and compound closures; DHS and FBI release JAR-16-20296A

rows.t: ProFTPD mod_copy, CVE-2015-3306: Unauthenticated File Copy in the Lab
ev: Bug 4169 filed; the fix is merged twelve minutes later and backported to 1.3.5
Exploit-DB 36742, ProFTPd 1.3.5 File Copy, published
CVE-2015-3306 assigned; the flaw disclosed on oss-security
Disclosure date of the Metasploit module proftpd_modcopy_exec
ProFTPD 1.3.5a released
Related flaw CVE-2019-12815 published
CISA adds CVE-2015-3306 to KEV; joint advisory AA26-281A lists it
Lab run: the vulnerable build copies a file without login; the fixed build refuses

rows.t: Russia-Attributed Threat Actors: The Public Record
ev: First public APT28 report
BlackEnergy attack on Ukraine's grid; 230,000 people without power
GRIZZLY STEPPE joint analysis report on APT28 and APT29
NotPetya
Indictment of 12 GRU officers for 2016 election interference
Indictment of six GRU officers in the Western District of Pennsylvania
US formal attribution of SolarWinds to the SVR; Treasury sanctions
Viasat KA-SAT disruption about an hour before the invasion
AA23-129A on Snake (FSB Center 16)
Mandiant graduates Sandworm to APT44
Poland energy attack: RTUs damaged at more than 30 wind and PV farms
UK and EU formally attribute the Poland attack to FSB Centre 16; first joint cyber sanctions

rows.t: Cyber Operations as Statecraft: The Cases in The Hacker and the State
ev: APT1's observed compromises begin, per Mandiant
First known adversarial access to the US Office of Personnel Management (OPM)
Shamoon wipes systems at a Saudi energy company (30,000 or more, per Unit 42)
Mandiant publishes APT1 and assesses it as PLA Unit 61398
Five PLA Unit 61398 officers indicted for economic espionage (announced 19 May)
The Sony Pictures wiper attack and the "Hacked By #GOP" screen
The FBI attributes the Sony attack to North Korea; US-CERT publishes TA14-353A
Bangladesh Bank loses about $81 million through fraudulent SWIFT messages
March to June 2016: GRU phishing, implants and theft at the Clinton campaign, the DCCC and the DNC
3 April to 3 May 2017: GRU spearphishing of the French presidential campaign
The US and five partner governments attribute WannaCry to North Korea
Twelve GRU officers indicted over the 2016 election hacking

rows.t: APT41: The Public Record, 2012 to 2026
ev: FireEye traces APT41 activity to 2012, when members targeted the video game industry
NetSarang's nssock2.dll backdoored in five software packages
ASUS Live Update compromise (ShadowHammer), June to November 2018; stage 1 unconfirmed as APT41
FireEye publishes APT41: A Dual Espionage and Cyber Crime Operation
A D.C. grand jury indicts Zhang Haoran and Tan Dailin
Indictment of Jiang, Qian and Fu over the Chengdu 404 racketeering conspiracy
CISA AA20-275A names APT41 exploiting Citrix NetScaler and Cisco routers
Campaign C0017 compromises at least six US state government networks, to February 2022
The US Secret Service says APT41 stole at least $20 million in COVID relief benefits
APT41 DUST (C0040) reported: prolonged access at shipping and logistics organizations
Google renames APT41 to SPIRE CASTLE
BlackX UEFI bootkit reported at diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan

rows.t: Iran-Attributed Threat Actors: The Public Record
ev: Coordinated DDoS attacks on the US financial sector begin (2011 to 2013), later charged against ITSecTeam and Mersad staff
Shamoon wiper first used, by a group calling itself Cutting Sword of Justice
Nine Mabna Institute members announced as indicted; Treasury sanctions the Institute the same day
AA20-259A: an Iran-based actor exploits Pulse Secure, Citrix and F5 flaws
A Fortigate appliance is exploited to reach the environmental control networks of a US children's hospital
Destructive attack on the Government of Albania begins; HomeLand Justice claims it on 18 July
Treasury designates MOIS and Minister Esmail Khatib over the Albania attack
At least 75 Unitronics PLC and HMI devices compromised to January 2024, 34 of them in US water and wastewater
AA24-241A on Pioneer Kitten's access brokering for ransomware affiliates
Tampering with internet-exposed Rockwell, Schneider Electric and Siemens PLCs begins (AA26-097A)
Stryker reports a global disruption to its Microsoft environment; Handala claims a wiper attack
Superseding indictment of 17 Mabna Institute members for intrusions for the IRGC since 2013

rows.t: Sandworm: The Operations in the Public Record
ev: MS14-060 patched; CVE-2014-4114 had been exploited in a Sandworm campaign
First Ukrainian blackout: three distribution companies, about 225,000 customers
Industroyer attack on a Kyiv transmission substation; about one hour of disruption
NotPetya spreads worldwide from the M.E.Doc update server
Bad Rabbit watering-hole ransomware
Olympic Destroyer wiper pushed during the opening ceremony
VPNFilter disclosed: at least 500,000 devices in at least 54 countries
About 15,000 Georgian websites defaced; broadcasters interrupted
Indictment of six Unit 74455 officers filed
Industroyer2 planned against high-voltage substations; CERT-UA says it was prevented
Third Ukrainian blackout, 10 to 12 October
Mandiant designates APT44

rows.t: The Zero-Day Trade and Its Fallout: The Events in This Is How They Tell Me the World Ends
ev: Google detects a targeted attack from China on its corporate infrastructure (Operation Aurora)
Google discloses the intrusion and says it will stop censoring Google.cn
Google announces Project Zero
Hacking Team breach becomes public; Flash CVE-2015-5119 and CVE-2015-5122 made public
The Shadow Brokers appear, claiming Equation Group files
Citizen Lab and Lookout publish Trident and Pegasus; Apple ships iOS 9.3.5 the next day
Microsoft publishes MS17-010
The Shadow Brokers release the Windows archive (15 April in the FBI affidavit)
WannaCry Version 2 spreads with the SMB worm; the kill-switch domain is registered
NotPetya arrives through the M.E.Doc updater
Citizen Lab reports FORCEDENTRY; Apple ships iOS 14.8
NSO Group, Candiru, Positive Technologies and a Singapore firm added to the Entity List

rows.t: North Korea-Attributed Threat Actors: The Public Record
ev: Destructive attack on Sony Pictures Entertainment; the FBI names the North Korean government on 19 December 2014
Bangladesh Bank SWIFT heist, $81 million (Treasury, 2018)
WannaCry ransomware; at least 81 NHS trusts in England disrupted; UK attribution to Lazarus Group on 19 December 2017
Federal complaint against Park Jin Hyok, an alleged RGB hacker
Treasury designates Lazarus Group, Bluenoroff and Andariel under E.O. 13722
Maui ransomware encrypts servers at a Kansas hospital; AA22-187A warns the health sector in July 2022
Ronin bridge theft, $620 million; the FBI attributes it to Lazarus Group and APT38 on 14 April 2022
State, Treasury and FBI guidance on thousands of North Korean IT workers posing as non-North Koreans
Indictment of Rim Jong Hyok of Andariel for ransomware against US hospitals; AA24-207A follows the next day
Bybit theft, about $1.5 billion; the FBI names TraderTraitor on 26 February 2025
Operation Lonestar Roundup searches of Texas laptop farms (21 to 25 September), announced 13 October 2026
Binance theft, more than $6 billion; the FBI names TraderTraitor on 31 October 2026, an attribution disputed in press

rows.t: China-Attributed Threat Actors: The Public Record
ev: Google discloses a targeted attack from China that stole intellectual property
Mandiant's APT1 report ties APT1 to PLA Unit 61398
Indictment of five Unit 61398 officers, 31 counts
BAE Systems attributes Operation Cloud Hopper against MSPs to APT10
Four PLA 54th Research Institute members charged over Equifax
Microsoft attributes Exchange zero-day exploitation to HAFNIUM
The US with the EU, UK and NATO names MSS-affiliated actors for the Exchange campaign
AA24-038A: high confidence that Volt Typhoon is pre-positioning for OT disruption
Seven APT31-linked nationals charged; OFAC sanctions Wuhan XRZ
Media first report Salt Typhoon in US telecoms
12 people charged, including eight i-Soon employees and APT27 actors
AA25-239A: 23 agencies in 13 countries on Salt Typhoon

rows.t: Stuxnet: The Case Study
ev: Stuxnet 0.5 C&C server registration
Stuxnet 0.5 submitted to a public scanning service
First initial infection, 12 hours after compile
Stuxnet driver signed with a valid Realtek certificate
VirusBlokAda reports the threat
Microsoft Security Advisory 2286198 on the LNK flaw
MS10-046 published
About 100,000 infected hosts, about 60 percent of them in Iran
CrySyS Duqu report: Stuxnet code massively reused
New York Times Olympic Games account, relayed by the Guardian
Coded infection stop date for Stuxnet 1.x
Symantec publishes Stuxnet 0.5: The Missing Link

rows.t: Other State-Linked Threat Actors: The Public Record
ev: Kaspersky reports Darkhotel's hotel-network delivery, Flash zero-days and certificate abuse
Citizen Lab reports Stealth Falcon's macro documents and PowerShell backdoor
Sea Turtle DNS hijacking through registrars and registries begins, to early 2019
Mandiant report on APT32
Lookout and EFF report on Dark Caracal
Talos publishes Sea Turtle, naming seven CVEs
Meta takedown links APT32 to CyberOne Group
Mandiant links UNC1151 to the Belarusian government
ESET reports MoustachedBouncer against foreign embassies in Belarus
Kaspersky reports SideWinder using CVE-2017-11882 and StealerBot
Stealth Falcon uses CVE-2025-33053 as a zero-day against a defense organization in Türkiye (Reported)
CVE-2025-33053 added to KEV and published by NVD

rows.t: United States-Attributed Threat Actors: The Public Record
ev: Earliest Regin sample timestamps
Stuxnet discovered
CrySyS publishes its Duqu analysis
Kaspersky discloses Flame
Kaspersky publishes its Regin analysis: 27 victims in 14 countries
Kaspersky discloses the Equation group
The Shadow Brokers post a sample archive they say came from Equation Group
Microsoft publishes MS17-010, fixing CVE-2017-0143 to CVE-2017-0148
WannaCry spreads with the EternalBlue exploit; NHS bodies in England are hit
The White House publishes the unclassified VEP charter
Kaspersky discloses Operation Triangulation; the FSB blames US intelligence the same day
China's Ministry of State Security alleges an NSA campaign against the National Time Service Center

rows.t: Kevin Mitnick: Ghost in the Wires and The Art of Intrusion
ev: Guilty plea to possessing 16 unauthorized MCI codes and computer fraud for copying a DEC security program (Reported)
Fugitive intrusion series against technology companies begins, after a warrant for violating the 1989 supervised release
IP-spoofing and session-hijack intrusion on Shimomura's systems; his account names no attacker
Shimomura posts the technical details of the Christmas Day attack to Usenet
Mitnick arrested in North Carolina
Ninth Circuit upholds the sentence and the bar on computers and cellular phones during supervised release
Global plea: four counts of wire fraud, two of computer fraud, one of intercepting a wire communication
Sentenced to 46 months, 68 months combined, with restitution of just over $4,125
Released; supervised release runs to 20 January 2003
Testifies to the Senate Committee on Governmental Affairs on pretext calls and weak callbacks
CISA and FBI publish AA23-320A on Scattered Spider's help desk impersonation
HHS HC3 analyst note on social engineering of health sector IT help desks

rows.t: Five Hacks and Why They Worked: The Cases in Fancy Bear Goes Phishing
ev: The Morris worm is released from an MIT computer at about 8:30 p.m. and spreads through sendmail, fingerd, trusted hosts and guessed passwords
The Dark Avenger releases his first virus from Sofia, begun in September 1988
The judgment against Morris sets three years probation, 400 hours of community service and a $10,050 fine
The Dark Avenger's Mutation Engine (MtE) lets any virus mutate through one subroutine
A Massachusetts juvenile is sentenced to 11 months for entry to an ISP and a telephone provider, accounts at an identity-data company and a denial of service
GRU Unit 26165 phishes the Clinton campaign chairman with a spoofed Google notice; over 50,000 emails taken
The DNC announces the Russian intrusion; CrowdStrike names two actors, APT29 and APT28
Over 20,000 DNC emails and documents released, about three days before the convention
Mirai hits Krebs on Security with a 623 Gbps attack
The Dyn attack, which the USENIX paper attributes to Mirai cluster 6, not the original cluster 1
Informations and plea agreements against three Mirai and clickfraud defendants filed in Alaska
Twelve GRU officers indicted in the District of Columbia over the 2016 intrusions and leaks

rows.t: The Cuckoo's Egg Intrusion: Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory, 1986
ev: At least five diskettes handed over in East Berlin from May to November 1986 (DER SPIEGEL, Reported)
LBL's accounting program fails to balance: a new account with no billing address
US request for help reaches the Deutsche Bundespost (DER SPIEGEL, Reported)
Alarmed SDI bait files hold the intruder for more than an hour while the trace to West Germany completes
Stoll's "Stalking the Wily Hacker" published in Communications of the ACM
Internet worm released; Stoll posts one of the first public warnings on RISKS
CERT/CC established by DARPA at the SEI, Carnegie Mellon
Three arrests after house searches; the Interior Ministry confirms the suspects supplied the KGB (Reported)
Three hackers indicted on espionage charges (AP, Reported)
Stoll posts the details of his book The Cuckoo's Egg (Doubleday, 1989)
Court in Celle gives Carl, Hess and Brzezinski suspended sentences (Reported)
RFC 1244 frames "Protect and Proceed" against "Pursue and Prosecute" and cites both Stoll works

rows.t: Cybercrime and Hacktivism in Four Books: Kingpin, Fatal System Error, We Are Anonymous, The Hacker Crackdown
ev: AT&T long-distance crash from its own 4ESS software update, at first suspected to be hackers
Secret Service searches Steve Jackson Games and seizes the Illuminati BBS
Operation Sundevil, 7 to 8 May 1990: about 27 warrants, 150 agents, 13 cities
Neidorf trial, 23 to 27 July 1990: the prosecution moves to dismiss and a mistrial is declared (Reported)
Fifth Circuit affirms Steve Jackson Games: seizing stored unread e-mail is not an intercept
Shadowcrew indictment and Operation Firewall's 28 arrests announced
Russian court sentences three bookmaker DDoS extortionists to eight years each (Reported)
Max Butler sentenced to 13 years and $27.5 million restitution
HBGary Federal breach: SQL injection, cracked and reused passwords, hijacked mail
FBI approaches Monsegur, who agrees to cooperate that night (about this date)
Jeremy Hammond sentenced to 10 years for computer hacking conspiracy
Monsegur sentenced to time served
